ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left side is the primary coil of the ideal transformer, connected to an AC power supply, with n1 marked beside it; the right side is the secondary coil, marked with n2. On the right side of the secondary coil, resistor R0 is first connected in series, and then it reaches the upper and lower two busbars; voltmeter V is connected across these two busbars, and R1 is vertically connected between the two busbars; on the right side there is also R2 vertically connected between the two busbars, but its upper end is connected into the circuit through switch S. Then reason: the primary coil is connected to a fixed AC voltage u=311sin(100πt) V, and the turns ratio of the ideal transformer is fixed, so the effective value U2 of the secondary-coil output voltage is fixed. The voltmeter ideally does not shunt current. When S is closed, the total load on the secondary side is equivalent to R0 in series with (R1∥R2); after S is opened, the R2 branch is removed, and the total load on the secondary side becomes R0+R1. Since R1∥R2<R1, after the switch is opened the equivalent total resistance on the secondary side increases. When the secondary-side voltage U2 is fixed, the transformer output power P=U2^2/R equivalent, so the increase in equivalent resistance makes the output power decrease.
